rationale: Jesus' instruction names the Mosaic provision directly -- "go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them" (8:4, BSB) -- without quoting its wording, which is why this is explicit_reference rather than quotation. The referent is not in doubt: Leviticus 14 opens "This is the law for the one afflicted with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing, when he is brought to the priest" (14:2, BSB) and prescribes the offerings for that day, including a cheaper set for one who "is poor and cannot afford these offerings" (14:21, BSB); Ellicott (citing 14:10 and 14:21-22), Barnes (14:2, 14:4) and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (14:1-57) all identify this chapter as the gift Matthew means. Two wording notes, checked against this app's text: Matthew's BSB wording is "offer the gift prescribed by Moses," while Mark 1:44 and Luke 5:14 read "present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing"; and the BSB of Leviticus 13-14 says "skin disease," not "leprosy," for the condition the BSB of Matthew 8:2-3 calls leprosy.
